conventions.dates: ISO; precision as sourced. Point observations have from == to. Statute-administration intervals are half-open [from, to) using the approval date of the charging and superseding orders; "from": null means start unknown (not nonexistent).

relations.minister_responsible_for: explicit statement or statutory administration order (see notes "Basis")
relations.appoints_to: Lieutenant-Governor in Council appointment; office = recommending minister on the OIC
relations.report_tabled_by: minister who presented the annual report to the House
relations.regulated_by: regulatory approvals under the provincial Railway Act
relations.budget_approval_recommended_by: minister recommending LGIC approval of Board salary lists/estimates/superannuation fund
relations.statutory_reporting_to: statute requires a specific report to the minister
relations.designation_basis_statement: statement about how the responsible minister is chosen (no holder asserted)
relations.complaints_and_referrals_via: minister receiving complaints / empowered to refer questions to an inquiry

subject_ids.pacific-great-eastern-railway: to 1972-04-01 (name change to British Columbia Railway Company, BC Archives authority record 1955/3371)
subject_ids.bc-railway-company: from 1972-04-01; note 1984-06-19 the company became a holding company for BC Rail Ltd. and BCR Properties Ltd. (BC Archives 3371); OICs 1997-2001 style it "British Columbia Railway Corporation"

intervals.locator: Order in Council 2813/1918 (BC Laws historical OIC archive, scanned PDF; quote from OCR text layer)
intervals.quote: in the matter of the PACIFIC GREAT EASTERN RAILWAY °MANY the sum of Thirty thousand dollars ... be paid to the above Company out of the monies deposited ... to the credit of the Minister of Finance
intervals.notes: Point observation (dated 23 Dec 1918; approval day illegible in OCR). Payment to the PGE under the 1916 loan statute (c. 38) recommended by the Minister of Finance; the attached estimate is marked approved by the "Minister of Railways". Evidence of provincial funding routed through Finance; not evidence of a designated responsible minister. Holder not named on the document; Finance was held by J. Hart and Railways by J. Oliver on that date per LLBC Executive Council Appointments PDF p. 43.

intervals.locator: Order in Council 644/1932 (BC Laws historical OIC archive, scanned PDF; quote from OCR text layer)
intervals.quote: THAT the resignation of WILLARD KITCHEN, Esquire, of Vancouver, as a Director of the Pacific Great Eastern Railway Company, be accepted. Dated this 1st day of June, A.D. 1932. ... Minister of Railways.
intervals.notes: Point observation. Appointing/accepting authority is the Lieutenant-Governor in Council; office recorded is the RECOMMENDING minister. Holder from LLBC Executive Council Appointments (execouncil.pdf PDF p. 48: Railways 21 Aug 1928 - 15 Nov 1933, S.F. Tolmie, who was also Premier).

intervals.locator: Order in Council 1506/1933 (BC Laws historical OIC archive, scanned PDF; quote from OCR text layer)
intervals.quote: pursuant to subsection (3) of Section 4 of the "Pacific Great Eastern Settlement Act," ... THE HONOURABLE THOMAS DUFFERIN PATTULLO, of Victoria, British Columbia, Premier and Minister of Railways ... HONOURABLE JOHN HART ... Minister of ... Finance
intervals.notes: Point observation (approved 13 Dec 1933; OCR year partly garbled). Recommended by the Minister of Railways (signature line "...mister of Railways"). The Premier-and-Minister-of-Railways (Pattullo) and the Minister of Finance (Hart) were themselves appointed PGE directors: ministers sat on the company board. Directors are appointed by the Lieutenant-Governor in Council under s. 4 of the Pacific Great Eastern Settlement Act, 1918.

intervals.locator: Order in Council 4018/1972 (BC Laws historical OIC archive, scanned PDF; quote from OCR text layer)
intervals.quote: "Railway Act", the Minister of Commercial Transport has approved an application of the British Columbia Railway Company for leave to construct a grade level crossing of Highway No. 97
intervals.notes: Regulatory relation (safety/crossing approvals under the provincial Railway Act), NOT ministerial responsibility for the company. Exact approval day not extracted. BC Archives (Railway Dept. authority record) states the Railway Dept. regulated railways under the provincial Railway Act 1911-1959, after which its functions went to the Dept. of Commercial Transport.

intervals.locator: Order in Council 3667/1972 (BC Laws historical OIC archive, scanned PDF; quote from OCR text layer)
intervals.quote: the following appointments be made to the Board of Directors of the British Columbia Railway Company: ,cs The Honourable D. Barrett, President and Chairman ... The Honourable W. King, Director and Executive Vice-President ... MINISTER OF FINANCE
intervals.notes: Approved 12 Oct 1972. Recommended by the Minister of Finance (Barrett was Premier and Minister of Finance, execouncil.pdf PDF p. 67). Rescinds the 1952/1957/1967 PGE-era director appointments of W.A.C. Bennett, E.M. Gunderson, R.G. Williston and J.J. Behan. Barrett personally became company President/Chairman (corporate office).

Evidence is limited to recommending ministers on director OICs (Minister of Railways 1932-1933; Minister of Finance 1942, 1970; Premier 1954, 1957) and a 1918 funding OIC. Signatures on OICs 342/47, 640/48, 2022/52, 29/61 and 3926/67 are illegible, so recommending office for those is unknown.

PGE annual reports and their transmittal/tabling (1918-1971) and WCB annual reports 1917-1973 (BC Sessional Papers, UBC Open Collections items e.g. 1.0059873, 1.0224414) could not be read: open.library.ubc.ca blocked automated access ("unusual activity"). Letters of transmittal / report_tabled_by for those years are therefore missing.
No pre-1972 Hansard exists (full Hansard began 1972); Journals of the Legislative Assembly were not consulted.

BCR 1972-1985: the instrument assigning administration of the British Columbia Railway Act to the Ministry of Transportation and Highways (in force by Feb 1985) was not found; start date of that interval is unknown. Pre-1979 statutory assignment (e.g. to Transport and Communications or Energy, Transport and Communications) not found.

BCR designated-minister intervals (Premier's designation, 1976-1986) are known only from Hansard observations, not from designation instruments; intervals between observations are not asserted. Observation dates: Economic Development/Phillips 1976-04-26 to 1978-06-28; ISBD/Phillips 1980-12-09 to 1982-10-05 (plus OICs to 1984-11-28); Heinrich 1986-05-06 to 1986-06-02. Who was designated between 11 Feb and 16 Apr 1986, and for 1978-06-28 to 1980-12-09 and 1982-10-05 to 1986-05-06, is unknown.

BCR 1987-1991 (Vander Zalm/Johnston): no Hansard statement explicitly naming a "minister responsible for B.C. Rail" was found by the scan; the record rests on statute-administration OICs and director OICs recommended by the Minister of Transportation and Highways.

The LLBC vanderzalmcabinet.pdf, harcourtcabinet.pdf, clarkcabinet.pdf, johnstoncabinet.pdf, millercabinet.pdf, dosanjhcabinet.pdf and campbell_cabinet.pdf contain NO "Minister Responsible for BC Rail" designation (text-searched); the backlog hint that vanderzalmcabinet.pdf lists one was not confirmed. LLBC cabinet lists for W.A.C. Bennett, Barrett and W.R. Bennett were not found at guessed URLs; the 1871-1986 Executive Council Appointments volume was used instead.
Several OIC approval dates are only partially legible in the OCR (e.g. 785/86, 1951/86, 651/96, 1162/95); precision was reduced or the legible drafting/Chambers date used, as noted per record.

WCB 1917-1935: no Minister of Labour recommendation found; WCB matters were recommended by the Attorney-General (1917, 1925) and Provincial Secretary (1922-1926 salary lists). Whether the Workmen's Compensation Act 1916 itself named a responsible minister was not checked (historical statute text not retrieved).
WCB Sloan 1952 and Tysoe 1966 commission reports (WorkSafeBC historical reports) were located but not read.

BC Rail sale 2003-2004 roles (e.g. Minister of Finance G. Collins; K. Falcon from 26 Jan 2004) are outside the requested window and not researched beyond one 2004 Hansard observation seen in the scan.
